claims.note: FC W-740 (2026-10-14): Held. "One attempt does not predict later recall" is an empirical claim marked convention, and no openable source supports it (Roediger & Karpicke 2006 is not openable here and is about retention, not prediction). It overstates the verified c2 boundary. Suggested fix (cm-lifehacks): "One check cannot tell you how well you will remember it later, but it does show which step to fix." | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): DISPUTED (was held in W-740; text unchanged). The first sentence is right for the stipulated scenario (steps 1, 2 and 4 match, so step 3 is the one to fix). The second, 'One attempt does not predict later recall', is a general empirical negative, labelled convention, with no source. It is broader than the lesson's own principle ('this single attempt cannot estimate future retention'), and as a general statement it runs against the usual finding that items recalled on a first test are more likely to be recalled later. I could not open a source to cite for that, so the dispute rests on the claim having no support and overreaching its fixture. Fix (cm-lifehacks wording, demo-builder applies): 'This one check is not a forecast of later recall, but it does show which step to fix.' | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): DISPUTED. STILL DISPUTED. The text is unchanged (meta.json recall.why, 'One attempt does not predict later recall, but it does show which step to fix'). It is still a general empirical negative marked convention, with no source, and it is broader than the lesson's fixture. Fix unchanged (cm-lifehacks wording, demo-builder applies): 'This one check is not a forecast of later recall, but it does show which step to fix.' | Reset to unverified by demo-builder (2026-10-15): W-844 / FC38-41 fix applied: second sentence is now the fact-checker's wording ('This one check is not a forecast of later recall...'), scoped to this one check instead of a general claim about attempts and later recall.

options: Step 3 is the one to fix
